risks.title: Spend structured to stay just below the quote threshold
risks.description: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.25000.rows}} payments worth {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.25000.gbp|gbp}} sit in the band just below the {{$.thresholds.quote_threshold.value|gbp}} quote threshold, and {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.25000.groups}} groups of two or more payments to one supplier within {{$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.window_days}} days each stay under that threshold while their total reaches it. Both patterns are indicators that a requirement may have been divided or valued to avoid three quotes via the Portal [rule:CPR-65] and the rule against splitting [rule:CPR-13]. Many groups are recurring care and education placement payments, which the auditor should expect to explain a share of the flags.

likelihood.justification: L4: two different tests flag the same risk, payments clustered just below the quote threshold [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.25000.rows] and payment groups crossing it [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.25000.groups]; only part of the split groups share one payment run [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.25000.same_timestamp_groups], so analytics.json does not explain the rest away. The Reasonable Assurance opinion on Contract Letting argues the other way [history:A-01] but does not move the rubric row.

impact.justification: C3: the flagged items sit in the tier from the quote threshold up to the intranet Threshold, where three quotes via the Procurement Portal are required [rule:CPR-65] [rule:CPR-67]; row C4 does not apply because the Threshold-tied tiers were not tested.

risks.proposed_focus: Pull the clustered payments and the split groups in the general procurement and premises tags first; for each, request the quote record via the Portal [rule:CPR-65] and ask whether the payments form one requirement under the anti-splitting rule [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-14]. Treat recurring placement invoices as a lower-priority stratum.

risks.title: Spend kept at or just below the one-quote level
risks.description: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.1000.rows}} payments worth {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.1000.gbp|gbp}} sit just at or below {{$.thresholds.tiers[0].value|gbp}}, and {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.1000.groups}} same-supplier payment groups each stay under that level while their total exceeds it. Above that level at least one quote is required [rule:CPR-64]; the patterns are indicators to test against the anti-splitting rule [rule:CPR-13].

likelihood.justification: L4: two different tests flag the same risk, clustering just below the one-quote level [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.1000.rows] and same-supplier groups crossing it [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.1000.groups]; some groups share one payment run [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.1000.same_timestamp_groups], which leaves most unexplained. Contract Letting was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-01].

impact.justification: C2: the flagged items sit below the quote threshold, in the band where one quote is sought [rule:CPR-64].

risks.proposed_focus: Sample clustered payments and split groups outside the placement tags and request the single quote or written purchase evidence for each [rule:CPR-64] [rule:CPR-35].

risks.title: Payment groups crossing the Key Decision and Executive approval levels
risks.description: {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.500000.groups}} same-supplier payment groups within {{$.tests.split_purchases.parameters.window_days}} days total at least {{$.thresholds.tiers[2].value|gbp}} while each payment stays below it, and {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.2500000.groups}} do the same at {{$.thresholds.tiers[3].value|gbp}}. Awards over the first level are Key Decisions [rule:CPR-04] [rule:CPR-60] and the second needs Executive approval [rule:CPR-62]. These tiers are noisy: instalments under existing term contracts and recurring placement fees can produce the pattern, and the tier £ figures double-count groups that appear at more than one tier.

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags groups at the higher tiers [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.500000.groups] [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.2500000.groups] and none of them share one payment run [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tier.500000.same_timestamp_groups], so analytics.json does not explain them away. Clustering below these levels flagged nothing [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.by_tier.500000.rows], so row L4 does not apply. Contract Letting was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-01].

impact.justification: C4: the flagged groups are at the Key Decision level and above, where the award must be a Key Decision [rule:CPR-04] or go to the Executive [rule:CPR-62].

risks.proposed_focus: For each higher-tier group, identify the contract the payments are made under and request the Key Decision or Executive approval record for the award [rule:CPR-04] [rule:CPR-60] [rule:CPR-62]; close groups that trace to an approved term contract.

risks.title: Suppliers above the publication threshold with no live Contracts Finder notice
risks.description: Outside care and education placements, which R-08 covers, suppliers whose annualised estimate reaches {{$.thresholds.publication_threshold.value|gbp}} and have no live notice matched by exact normalised name are: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.general_procurement}} in general procurement ({{$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.general_procurement|gbp}} in the window), {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.grant}} grant recipients ({{$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.grant|gbp}}), {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.premises}} premises suppliers ({{$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.premises|gbp}}) and {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.agency_staff}} agency staff supplier ({{$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.agency_staff|gbp}}); {{$.tests.off_contract.with_candidate_name}} suppliers across the full list have a near-miss candidate name listed separately. Grants stay in this risk: the auditor's scope decision keeps them here to be tested. Contracts at this level need a published notice [rule:CPR-66] and quotes via the Portal [rule:CPR-65]. The notice export starts in 2021 and matching is by name only, so 'no notice found' is a prompt to request contract evidence, not evidence that none exists.

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags suppliers above the publication threshold with no live notice outside the placement tag, in general procurement [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.general_procurement], grants [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.grant], premises [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.premises] and agency staff [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.agency_staff]; analytics.json does not explain them away. Narrowing the population to these tags leaves the same single test, so the rubric row does not move. The Reasonable Assurance opinion on Contract Letting argues the other way [history:A-01].

impact.justification: C3: the narrowed population still sits from the publication threshold up, the tier where a notice on the CDP and three Portal quotes are required [rule:CPR-66] [rule:CPR-65], across general procurement, grant, premises and agency staff suppliers [metric:$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.general_procurement] [metric:$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.grant]; row C4 would need the Threshold-tied rules, which were not tested, so the narrowing does not move the rubric row.

risks.proposed_focus: Test the no-live-notice suppliers outside the care and education placement tag: general procurement first, then grants, premises and agency staff, plus the near-miss candidates. For each, request the contract or grant agreement, its award notice [rule:CPR-66] and its entry on the contracts register [rule:CPR-07]. Leave placement suppliers to R-08. Do not question suppliers below the publication threshold.

risks.title: Payments to suppliers whose every matched notice ended before the spend window
risks.description: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.total}} suppliers, paid {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp.total|gbp}} in the window, match only notices that ended before the window started. An extension provided for in a contract needs S151 approval [rule:CPR-76]; a newer contract with no notice may also explain the payments.

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags suppliers paid after every matched notice ended [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.total] [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.gbp.total], and analytics.json records no benign pattern for them. Contract Letting was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-01].

impact.justification: C3: the matched notices are Contracts Finder awards, published from the quote threshold tier [rule:CPR-66], and continuing to pay needs an approved extension [rule:CPR-76]; no metric places the flagged items at the Key Decision level, so row C4 does not apply.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged supplier, request the S151 extension approval [rule:CPR-76] or the current contract and its award record [rule:CPR-38].

risks.title: Annualised spend above the awarded contract value without a recorded variation
risks.description: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.total}} of {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.eligible_suppliers}} suppliers matched to one live single-supplier notice show an annualised estimate at least {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.parameters.ratio_flag}} times the award's annual value. A variation of scope or value needs prior approval [rule:CPR-77] [rule:CPR-78]. Award values may be estimates or maxima, and annualising a 3-month total can overstate a lumpy year.

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags spend beyond the award's annual value [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.total] [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.gbp.total], with no benign pattern recorded in analytics.json. Contract Letting was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-01].

impact.justification: C3: the flagged contracts are published awards from the quote threshold tier upward [rule:CPR-66], and a variation needs Monitoring Officer and S151 approval [rule:CPR-77]; row C4 nearly applied because a variation above the Threshold goes to the relevant board [rule:CPR-78], but no metric tiers the flagged awards.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged supplier, compare actual spend to date with the award and request any variation approval [rule:CPR-77] [rule:CPR-78] or extension record [rule:CPR-76].

risks.title: Repeat payments of the same amount to the same supplier within a week
risks.description: {{$.tests.duplicates.different_dates.items}} supplier and amount pairs recur on different payment dates within {{$.tests.duplicates.parameters.window_days}} days, with a repeat value of {{$.tests.duplicates.different_dates.gbp_repeat_value|gbp}}; a further {{$.tests.duplicates.same_timestamp.items}} pairs recur within one payment run (repeat value {{$.tests.duplicates.same_timestamp.gbp_repeat_value|gbp}}), mostly per-client placement invoices at a standard rate. No Contract Procedure Rule sets this test; it is a payment-control indicator tied to the written evidence each purchase needs [rule:CPR-35]. The repeat value is an upper bound on money at stake, not a loss.

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags repeat amounts on different payment dates [metric:$.tests.duplicates.different_dates.items], which the one-payment-run pattern does not explain. The same-run repeats [metric:$.tests.duplicates.same_timestamp.items] read as payment runs and alone would sit at row L2. Accounts Payable was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-15].

impact.justification: Financial: the repeat value of different-date pairs [metric:$.tests.duplicates.different_dates.gbp_repeat_value] is the amount that could have been paid twice; it is an upper bound, since most pairs are placement fees for different clients [metric:$.tests.duplicates.different_dates.items_by_tag.care_education_placement].

risks.proposed_focus: Sample the different-date pairs, general procurement and premises first, and match each payment to a distinct invoice and purchase record [rule:CPR-35]; for placement pairs, confirm each payment relates to a different client or period.

risks.title: High-value care and education placements with no published contract notice
risks.description: {{$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.care_education_placement}} care and education placement suppliers above the publication threshold have no live notice, worth {{$.tests.off_contract.gbp.by_tag.care_education_placement|gbp}} in the window. Individual placements can be excluded from competition, but the reasons for the choice of provider must be on the case notes [rule:CPR-79] and Provider Selection Regime decisions recorded [rule:CPR-74].

likelihood.justification: L3: one test flags placement suppliers above the publication threshold with no live notice [metric:$.tests.off_contract.counts.by_tag.care_education_placement]; analytics.json does not explain them away. Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision was rated Reasonable Assurance [history:A-18], which argues the other way.

impact.justification: C3: the suppliers are at or above the publication threshold tier [rule:CPR-66], and the exclusion depends on a recorded provider choice [rule:CPR-79].

risks.proposed_focus: Sample placement suppliers from the list and request the case-note record of provider choice [rule:CPR-79], or the PSR decision record [rule:CPR-74], or the framework or block contract the placement sits under.

risks.title: Waivers and exceptions to the Rules not approved or recorded in advance
risks.description: Competition can be waived above the quote threshold only on urgency or Executive Director discretion with written reasons [rule:CPR-21] [rule:CPR-22], approved by the Monitoring Officer or S151 Officer [rule:CPR-23] and fully documented [rule:CPR-28]. No spend test can see a waiver; the evidence sits in council records.

likelihood.justification: L2: the evidence is council records only, since no spend test can see a waiver [rule:CPR-23] [rule:CPR-28], and the last audit on the theme, Contract Letting, was Reasonable Assurance [history:A-01]. Set by the auditor (decision R-09): high stakes bear on impact, not likelihood.

impact.justification: C3: the waiver rules apply from the quote threshold tier [rule:CPR-22]; exceptions above the Key Decision level go to the Executive [rule:CPR-27], which would be row C4, but no metric shows waivers at that level.

risks.proposed_focus: Request the waiver and exception register and test a sample for advance approval and written reasons [rule:CPR-24] [rule:CPR-30]; cross-check against suppliers flagged in the off-contract list [rule:CPR-66].

changes.note: Narrowed to no-live-notice suppliers outside the care_education_placement tag (R-08 covers placements); grants, premises and agency staff stay in and are cited by tag. Scores unchanged: L3 and C3 rows do not move.
Likelihood 3 to 2 as the auditor asked; justification cites the L2 row (council records only, last audit Reasonable).
